svg.text: SH-ESP32 proto area, BOTTOM view (solder side): two-NPN SeaTalk interface
Mirror image of seatalk-sh-esp32-npn-protolayout-v2.svg. Columns run T to A left to right; rows are unchanged. Board turned over left-to-right.
Solid coloured lines: solder these links on this side. Dashed outlines: parts on the far (top) side, shown where their leads come through.
GPIO header (seen from below; pins mirrored)
Links to solder on this side (join every hole listed)
SeaTalk DATA (yellow): B4–G4, G3–G4, H3–G3, G4–G6, G6–H6
R1 10 kΩ: C3, G3 R_b2 100 kΩ: H3, L3 R_pd2 22 kΩ (20 kΩ ok): M3, Q3
R_c 10 kΩ: H1, L1 R_b1 2.2 kΩ: I4, M4 R_pd1 10 kΩ: J5, N5
Q1 2N3904: C=H6 B=I6 E=J6 Q2 2N3904: C=L2 B=M2 E=N2 (flat face toward row 1 on both)
Wires: edge pads 3/4/5 to B3/B4/B5. K2 to GPIO27. N4 to GPIO26.
From this side each transistor reads E-B-C left to right (Q1: J6, I6, H6; Q2: N2, M2, L2). Letters are printed on the top only: count holes from the round corner pads.
H4 and H5 stay empty: they separate DATA from the Q1 base net. Check each link with a meter before fitting the next.
Before power-up: DATA (B4) to GND reads ~1 MΩ or more; 3.3 V to GND is not a short; GPIO27 (K2) to 3.3 V reads 10 kΩ;
DATA (B4) to +12 V (B3) reads ~10 kΩ. Then remove R_in and the old opto wiring from DATA.
